solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very bright having old Peruvian origin

parts.note: Incan describes the people of the old Peruvian empire
descent is ancestry or origin

explanation.surface: Something dazzling is said to come from an ancient Peruvian source.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing with intense heat and light, hence extremely bright or brilliant.

clue.text: Mean at home, see love suffering

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
V is the abbreviation for vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: suffering suggests the word love is damaged and knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A spiteful person at home watches a romance going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like an adjective (unkind) but is the verb: to entail. 'suffering' turns LOVE into OLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail or necessitate: if a job means travel it entails travel.

clue.text: Feline unable to admire last of autumn leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so this letter goes out of the phrase

parts.note: if you can't like something you are unable to admire it; the apostrophe is ignored

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word autumn

explanation.surface: Someone cannot bring themselves to admire the falling leaves at the end of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage in the autumn scene, but it is the verb: N, the last of autumn, departs from CANT LIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline as an adjective describes anything resembling a cat in grace or manner.

clue.text: Direction in which earth's not spinning

indicators.note: spinning sends the letters of earth's not whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which way the planet is not rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point, one of the bearings between two cardinal points.

clue.text: Makes rounded vases reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word for the vases is taken by its sound

parts.note: urns are rounded vases

explanation.surface: Someone produces bulbous pots, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to bring it in as income, as in 'she makes a fortune'.

clue.text: Last standing officer corrals large group

indicators.note: corrals means pens in, so the officer's name surrounds the letter

parts.note: General Custer was the officer of Custer's Last Stand at Little Bighorn
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: The final officer still on his feet rounds up a big herd.
explanation.walkthrough: Custer's Last Stand (1876) was the US cavalry defeat at Little Bighorn; 'corrals' suits the cowboy setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch or collection of similar things gathered close together, a near synonym.

clue.text: Falls back once more having run ahead to start with

indicators.note: back says the word for once more is written in reverse in this down clue

parts.note: again means once more

indicators.note: to start with picks the opening letters of run and ahead

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles over again, having dashed out in front at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border, a proper name for Falls.

clue.text: Wearing less than smart apparel invites criticism

definitions.meaning: to dress down is to wear clothes more casual than usual

explanation.surface: Turning up in scruffy clothes earns a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding is a sharp reprimand, the British idiom for a stern rebuke.

clue.text: Does it fascinate shipyard worker?

parts.note: to rivet means to fascinate, so one who rivets would fascinate; but literally a shipyard hand hammers rivets into plates

explanation.surface: A question about whether a dockyard labourer finds something gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fastens metal plates with rivets, as in shipbuilding.

clue.text: Plant rot

definitions.meaning: a garden plant with edible pink stalks
rot means nonsense, as in 'talking rot'

explanation.surface: A greenery suffering from decay.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable grown for its stalks, and also slang for nonsense or meaningless chatter.

clue.text: Fashionable bit with dusty hair and skin

indicators.note: fashionable is read as able to be fashioned, so the letters are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A trendy piece of kit with dirty hair and a complexion to match.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naked is wearing only the skin you were born in, a jokey idiom.

clue.text: Mercenary is flesh-wounded

indicators.note: wounded suggests the letters of is flesh have been hurt and pulled out of shape

explanation.surface: A hired soldier has taken a flesh wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercenary' looks like the noun for a hired soldier; here it is the adjective, motivated by gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercenary as an adjective means motivated purely by self-interest or money.

clue.text: Show on TV female with fine prospects

indicators.note: on means the word for show comes after the others in this across clue

parts.note: a TV is a television set
to air a programme is to show it

explanation.surface: A woman's programme airs on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecast phrase for settled conditions, extended to anything with good prospects.

clue.text: Woman from India with Frenchman

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A lady from India is accompanied by a man from France.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so a woman of that name.

clue.text: At the farm produced second crop

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A farm yields a second harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: The original sense: a second mowing of grass in a season, the later crop.

clue.text: Perplex with support for primitive type

parts.note: to throw someone is to disconcert or perplex them
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Confusing someone while also backing them up, for an old-fashioned sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversion to an earlier ancestral type, someone or something seemingly from a primitive past.

clue.text: Empty morphine into liquid storage tank

indicators.note: into says the emptied drug goes inside the rearranged letters
liquid means flowing, so the letters of storage are poured into a new order
empty means the word morphine is emptied of its inside, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: Pouring a drug into a container for storing fluids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid storage tank' reads as one phrase, but 'liquid' is the anagram signal and only 'tank' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large storage tank for gas, a gasholder.

clue.text: Bear cat in bag hunter's opening

indicators.note: in places the cat inside the bag

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch
a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of hunter's

explanation.surface: A hunter's bag holds a bear and a cat at its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal but is the verb: to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Skirt around black taxi

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
ca, short for circa, means around
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A short skirt wrapped round a black cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a containment instruction but gives CA (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: A British private-hire car booked by phone, as opposed to a black cab hailed in the street.

clue.text: Accountant keeps extravagant tunic for priest

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the accountant surrounds the extravagant letters

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
OTT is over the top, extravagant

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper holds on to an over-the-top garment for a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A short white surplice worn by clergy and choristers, a kind of tunic.

clue.text: Circle lake bed first

indicators.note: first means the bed comes before the lake

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Instructions for a lake circuit with the bed laid out first.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group, a social circle.

clue.text: Bad storm carrying on causes shakes

indicators.note: carrying says the rearranged storm holds the other piece within it
bad suggests the letters of storm are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A violent storm continuing makes everything tremble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying on' reads as one phrase meaning continuing; split it, so 'carrying' is the container signal and 'on' a separate piece. 'Bad' rearranges the storm into TMORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremors are shakes or quivers, and earth tremors are small shakes.

clue.text: Irish clan on about scam with gold

indicators.note: about means the word on goes round the scam

parts.note: a con is a scam
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A tale of an Irish family running a swindle for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The O'Connors are a historic Irish family, a clan descended from early kings.

clue.text: Trip across grand escarpment

indicators.note: across means the ride stretches over the other letter, holding it

parts.note: a ride is a trip
G is a grand, a thousand dollars or pounds

explanation.surface: A journey that cuts over a great steep slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A long raised ridge of land, often with a steep side, an escarpment.

clue.text: One observing written verses occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone watching poems being written now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker who sees an event happen, a bystander.

clue.text: Political party in nude dancing that's subtle

indicators.note: in says the party goes inside the rearranged letters
dancing means the letters of nude move about into a new order

parts.note: the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Politicians dancing naked, in a delicate way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges the nude letters into NUED; 'that's' merely links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing fine shades of meaning or distinction, hence subtle.

clue.text: Men arriving in time to fool one in theory

indicators.note: arriving in says the soldiers enter the middle of the date

parts.note: April Fools' Day is 1 April, written as APR I
one is the Roman numeral I
OR is other ranks, enlisted men

explanation.surface: Soldiers turn up at the right moment to trick someone.
explanation.walkthrough: April Fools' Day, 1 April, abbreviated as a date gives the time to fool; OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for men.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase for reasoning from theory rather than experience, deductively.

clue.text: These workers' benders are something special!

definitions.meaning: workers are the honey insects of a hive, and their benders are the leg joints that flex

explanation.surface: A boast that these labourers' knees are remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1920s idiom for the very best, an excellent person or thing.
